caption: F1. BMI–hypercapnia relationships at the first eligible adult 2022 acute-care encounter. ABG denotes PaCO₂ ≥45 mm Hg; ABG or VBG denotes PaCO₂ ≥45 or PvCO₂ ≥50 mm Hg. Gas curves standardize over outcome-evaluable patients; ICD uses known diagnosis capture. Model/ref N is the common model and reference count. Availability and BMI frequency use all adjustment-complete patients (C); the four frequency groups are mutually exclusive. Adjustment: age, sex, race/ethnicity, geographic region and encounter setting (EMER reference; IMP inpatient) with a fixed natural BMI spline. Shading and fine boundaries show pointwise model-based 95% CIs; dotted segments are locally sparse and dashed segments exceed training BMI support. Open availability points use Wilson intervals when no model is estimable. Known capture is distinct from ICD positivity. ABG/VBG: arterial/venous blood gas. Conditional model uncertainty excludes selection and measurement assumptions; no population transport or causal effect is inferred.

caption: F2. Paired scenario: One-unit BMI reduction for observed BMI >30; no floor. ABG: arterial PCO₂ ≥45 mm Hg; ABG or VBG: arterial ≥45 or venous ≥50 mm Hg; ICD: five-code composite including E66.2. Left: observed and shifted standardized probabilities with model-based 95% CIs and printed limits. Left axes share the full 0–1,000 reference-patient scale; printed probabilities and limits retain small differences. N identifies the common model/reference population; shifted percentage is a descriptive cohort fraction. Right: signed original-BMI-band contributions per 1,000 reference patients, with 95% CIs. Patients at BMI ≤30 remain in baseline burden and contribute exactly zero scenario difference; the eligible share is printed. Total-difference/PIF limits are printed; contribution covariance reproduces total variance. Right axes vary by outcome and retain zero and all limits. Gas samples are outcome-evaluable; ICD uses known capture. Adjustment, source-entry membership and covariates are fixed. PIF is the model-standardized potential impact fraction. These conditional scenarios do not estimate a weight-loss treatment effect.
